text.tspan: The Module Graph
Static imports are resolved before any of your code runs. Dynamic import() happens later, and returns a promise.
Static: import ... from '...'
main.js
cart.js
format.js
money.js
The whole graph is discovered and fetched first. Imports are
hoisted, so their position in the file does not matter. Each module
is evaluated exactly ONCE, however many files import it.
Dynamic: await import('...')
App starts: heavy module NOT loaded
User clicks something
const mod = await import('./chart.js')
Fetched now, then used
A function call, not a declaration, so it can sit inside an if,
take a computed path, and be awaited. This is code splitting.
ESM (import / export) is the standard, and the default everywhere. CommonJS (require / module.exports) is Node's older system:
require is synchronous and runs at the point it appears, which is exactly why import can be analysed ahead of time and require cannot.
In Node, .mjs or "type": "module" selects ESM; in the browser, <script type="module">.
